question: A DevOps team configures Claude with tool access to restart non-critical staging servers and open low-priority tickets automatically, while any action affecting production systems requires explicit human approval before execution. Is this an appropriate use of Claude?
options: A) No, because opening tickets automatically counts as a high-risk action needing professional review
B) No, because the Usage Policy prohibits granting Claude any tool access to servers under all circumstances
C) Yes, but only after Claude is also granted full, unreviewed access to production systems directly
D) Yes, because low-stakes automated actions are allowed while production changes need human approval
correct_answers: D) Yes, because low-stakes automated actions are allowed while production changes need human approval
explanations: Incorrect. Opening low-priority tickets in a staging environment is not the kind of high-risk domain, such as legal or healthcare, that triggers professional-review-and-disclosure requirements.
Incorrect. The Usage Policy does not prohibit tool access to servers outright; agentic tool use is a supported capability when scoped and overseen appropriately.
Incorrect. Removing human approval from production changes would increase risk rather than being a requirement; the described scenario is already appropriate as configured.
Correct. Allowing autonomous action on low-stakes staging tasks while requiring human approval for production changes reflects an appropriate, risk-proportionate use of agentic tool access.
